en.title: Chris Hansen Buys Ads to Counter Robert Pattinson's 'Primetime' Film
en.summary: Chris Hansen, the former host of 'To Catch a Predator,' is reportedly buying ad space before screenings of the upcoming A24 film 'Primetime,' which stars Robert Pattinson as Hansen. This move comes after Hansen's refusal to sign an NDA for an early screening of the film, which is based on an Esquire article about his past work.
en.body:
The man who once famously confronted suspected predators is now finding himself on the other side of the lens, and he's not happy about it. **Chris Hansen**, the indelible host of **To Catch a Predator**, is reportedly taking a rather unconventional approach to the upcoming A24 thriller **Primetime**. The film, which stars **Robert Pattinson** and is directed by **Lance Oppenheim** (known for **Spermworld**), is based on the Esquire article "Tonight On Dateline, This Man Will Die." Hansen, apparently displeased with how he might be portrayed, refused to sign a non-disclosure agreement that would have allowed him an advance screening.

Instead of letting the film speak for itself, Hansen has opted for a proactive, and some might say defiant, publicity stunt. According to The Hollywood Reporter, he has purchased advertising slots before every screening of **Primetime** through his own streaming network, TruBlu. These ads reportedly feature Hansen himself, addressing the audience and directing them to take a seat – a move that cleverly ties into his past work while promoting his current endeavors. This strategy offers a unique form of synergy, albeit one born from contention, that A24 might not be entirely opposed to, given the added buzz it generates.

## Hansen's Media Maneuvers

This latest development follows Hansen's appearance in **David Osit**'s media-crit documentary **Predators**. In that film, Hansen faced tough questions regarding media ethics from the former Dateline NBC anchor, questions he didn't appear fully prepared to answer. The irony of **Chris Hansen** now hawking his own crusader persona to promote his network, while simultaneously pursuing legal options against a film that might criticize him for building fame on that very persona, is a narrative loop that doesn't seem to be lost on observers. The film, humorously dubbed "Dark Knightcrawler" by some on social media, promises to delve into the complexities of Hansen's career and the methods he employed.

## The Stakes for Fans

For fans of true crime, media commentary, and perhaps even the schadenfreude of public figures battling their own narratives, **Primetime** and Hansen's reaction offer a compelling meta-story. It raises questions about how real-life figures engage with their fictionalized counterparts and the power dynamics at play when Hollywood adapts controversial careers. Will Hansen's preemptive advertising campaign boost his network or simply add fuel to the fire, making audiences even more curious about what the film will reveal? The situation underscores the blurred lines between reality TV, journalism, and cinematic interpretation, leaving viewers eager to see how this complex narrative unfolds both on screen and in the public sphere.

## What's Next

**Primetime** is set to premiere at the Venice International Film Festival before hitting theaters on September 25. Audiences will soon be able to judge for themselves how **Robert Pattinson** and **Lance Oppenheim** have depicted the world of **Chris Hansen** and his controversial legacy.

content_raw: Few of us will ever live the kind of lives that end up being adapted into a film starring a very handsome actor. Chris Hansen, host of the infamous reality TV series To Catch a Predator , will soon experience just that with Primetime , the upcoming thriller starring Robert Pattinson based on the Esquire article, “Tonight On Dateline, This Man Will Die.” And he’s seemingly furious. After refusing to sign an NDA with A24 to screen the film in advance, which might have shown him how Pattinson and director Lance Oppenheim ( Spermworld ) portrayed him and his reputation, Hansen is opting to keep giving the film free publicity, even while chipping in a few bucks of his own. According to The Hollywood Reporter , Hansen has purchased theater ads for his streaming network, TruBlu, which airs his latest efforts to corner suspected child molesters by first casually suggesting they park it somewhere. These spots, which feature Hansen addressing the theater audience and telling them to take a seat, will play before every screening of Primetimer —a form of synergy to which A24 is probably not entirely opposed.  These grievances come after David Osit’s media-crit documentary Predators , in which Hansen appeared in an interview that posed tough questions about media ethics the former Dateline NBC anchor didn’t seem fully prepared to answer. And indeed, the irony of hawking his crusader persona to promote his network while he pursues legal options against a film that may criticize Hansen for pursuing fame using that very persona is perhaps eluding Hansen at the moment.  Primetime , the film which punny folks on social media have called “ Dark Knightcrawler ,” will hit theaters on September 25 after its world premiere at the Venice International Film Festival on September 5.
